mainTopic: Dealing with people who are not careful about טומאה, מעשר and שביעית: grinding for them, leaving produce with them, and when we worry they switched our food
overview: This amud continues the discussion of the wife of a חבר grinding together with the wife of an עם הארץ. A ברייתא forbids grinding for people who eat their food in טומאה, and אביי explains that it means a כהן who eats תרומה in טומאה, a Torah-level sin. The גמרא then asks how that ברייתא can allow depositing produce with such a כהן. רבי אילעא suggests the produce is sealed in a clay vessel (צמיד פתיל), but this fails because his wife, while a נדה, could make it טמא just by moving it. So רבי ירמיה answers that depositing is allowed only for produce not yet made ready to receive טומאה. Next, a משנה about bringing wheat to an עם הארץ miller shows that we do not worry he switched the grain. The גמרא tests this against cases where we do worry about switching: a mother-in-law and an innkeeper. Each turns out to have a special personal motive. Finally, the גמרא asks whether ordinary people are really never suspected. It quotes a ברייתא with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's stricter view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids grinding for people who eat in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that allows grinding and depositing alongside people who eat שביעית produce or eat their food in טומאה, but forbids grinding for them. This seems to contradict רבא's reading of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may grind and deposit with those who eat שביעית produce, and with those who eat their own produce in טומאה. But one may not grind for those who eat שביעית produce, or for those who eat their own produce in טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבא's explanation of the משנה. The ברייתא says you may not grind for someone who eats his food in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explained that the wife of a חבר may grind together with the wife of an עם הארץ, even though the עם הארץ eats his food in טומאה. The ברייתא says you may not grind for such a person, because that would help him do something wrong. So the two seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: One may grind (grain into flour)
One may deposit, meaning leave something in someone's care
People who eat שביעית produce in a forbidden way
In a state of ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the small word change: 'אֵצֶל' (alongside / with) is allowed, but 'לְ' (for) is forbidden. Grinding your own food next to them is fine; grinding their food for them is not.

phrases.english: One may grind and deposit with those who eat Sabbatical-Year produce,
phrases.notes: This is your own properly tithed food. You may grind it at their place or leave it with them.

phrases.english: and with those who eat their own produce in impurity;
but not for those who eat Sabbatical-Year produce,
and not for those who eat their own produce in impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation of the משנה from the earlier part of the sugya.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that a חבר's wife may grind with the wife of an עם הארץ who eats in טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids grinding for people who eat their produce in טומאה, so helping such a person seems forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא is about a כהן eating תרומה in impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא is about a כהן suspected of eating תרומה in טומאה, which is forbidden by the Torah itself. That is why grinding for him is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There, we are dealing with a כהן who is suspected of eating תרומה in טומאה, which is a Torah-level טומאה prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the ברייתא is talking about a different, more serious case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain עם הארץ eating his own regular food in טומאה is not doing a Torah sin, so helping him is allowed. A כהן eating תרומה in טומאה breaks a Torah law, so you may not grind for him. The two sources talk about different people, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other source
We are dealing with
A כהן who is suspected (of doing something wrong)
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן
From the Torah itself

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how strict we are about helping someone depends on whether his wrongdoing is a Torah-level sin.

phrases.english: Abaye said: There,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא we just quoted.

phrases.english: with a priest who is suspected of eating teruma in impurity
we are dealing –
for which it is an impurity prohibition by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by moving the ברייתא to a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ברייתא is about a כהן and תרומה, not an ordinary person and ordinary food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids helping anyone who eats his food in טומאה, which would contradict רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids only helping a כהן who eats תרומה in טומאה, a Torah sin. Helping an ordinary עם הארץ is still allowed.

steps.title: How can you leave produce with such a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if the ברייתא is about a כהן, how can it allow depositing with him? Another ברייתא says you may not leave תרומה with a כהן who is an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, can one really deposit with him?! And a ברייתא contradicts it: One may deposit תרומה with a ישראל who is an עם הארץ, but not with a כהן who is an עם הארץ, because he is so used to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer. If the ברייתא is about a כהן, its first half, which allows depositing with him, now seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא allowed depositing produce with these people. Another ברייתא says you may not leave תרומה with a כהן who is an עם הארץ, because he is used to handling תרומה and will not be careful with it. So אביי's answer creates a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if your answer is right
And they pointed out a contradiction (from another source)
Someone not careful about purity laws
He is so used to it that he does not treat it with care

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not grinding but depositing. אביי's answer explained the grinding part, but it makes the depositing part of the same ברייתא hard to understand.

phrases.english: If so, may one deposit?!
phrases.notes: If it is about a כהן, how could the first ברייתא allow leaving produce with him?

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: מַפְקִידִין תְּרוּמָה אֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: One may deposit teruma with an Israelite who is an am ha'aretz,
but not with a priest who is an am ha'aretz,
because he is accustomed to it!
phrases.notes: Literally, 'his heart is coarse with it.' He is so used to תרומה that he would handle it and make it טמא.

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the first ברייתא is about a כהן suspected of eating תרומה in טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first ברייתא allows depositing with these people, but another ברייתא forbids depositing תרומה with a כהן who is an עם הארץ, because he will handle it carelessly.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: the produce is sealed in a clay vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא answers that the deposit is in a clay vessel sealed with a tight cover (צמיד פתיל). Such a vessel keeps out טומאה, so there is no worry about the כהן making it טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: What are we dealing with here? With a כלי חרס that has a tightly bound cover (צמיד פתיל).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא saves אביי's answer by explaining which kind of deposit the first ברייתא allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clay vessel closed with a tight lid cannot become טמא from the inside when someone touches it from the outside. So even if the כהן is careless, the produce inside stays pure. That is why depositing is allowed here, while the other ברייתא was about an open deposit.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
A vessel made of clay
A tightly bound cover that seals the vessel

steps.whatToRemember: Grinding for someone who sins against the Torah (a כהן eating תרומה in טומאה) is forbidden. רבי אילעא tries to explain the allowed deposit as a sealed clay vessel, but the next step challenges this answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a sealed clay vessel protects its contents from טומאה, so even someone who is not careful cannot make them טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
With what are we dealing here –
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the first ברייתא, which allowed depositing.

phrases.english: with an earthenware vessel enclosed with a tightly bound cover.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and keeps אביי's answer standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the deposit is sealed so that it cannot become טמא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Depositing with a כהן suspected about טומאה should be forbidden, as the second ברייתא says.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא allows depositing only in a sealed clay vessel, which he cannot make טמא. The second ברייתא is about an unsealed deposit.

steps.title: The wife could make the sealed vessel impure by moving it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי אילעא's sealed-vessel answer: a נדה makes things טמא by moving them, even inside a sealed vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should still worry that his wife, while she is a נדה, might move the vessel and make the produce טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילעא's answer from Step 4. A sealed vessel does not help if the כהן's wife, while a נדה, moves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צמיד פתיל blocks טומאה that comes from touching. But a נדה passes on טומאה just by moving an object (היסט), even a sealed one. So the sealed vessel does not fully remove the worry, and רבי אילעא's answer does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us worry, a way of raising a concern that was not addressed
Moving something; she will move it
A woman in her monthly period of impurity

phrases.english: But let us worry that his wife, as a נדה, might move it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אילעא's sealed-vessel answer from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's claim that a צמיד פתיל removes any worry of טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נדה passes on טומאה by moving an object (היסט), which a sealed vessel does not block.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: produce that is or is not ready to receive impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה drops the sealed-vessel answer. One ברייתא is about produce that is already able to become טמא, and the other is about produce that is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי ירמיה said: There is no difficulty. Here, the ברייתא forbidding it, is talking about produce that has become ready to receive טומאה. There, the ברייתא allowing it, is talking about produce that has not become ready to receive טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a new answer to the contradiction from Step 3. He says the two ברייתות are talking about different kinds of produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce can only become טמא after it has gotten wet with certain liquids (הכשר). If the produce was never made ready, the כהן or his wife cannot make it טמא at all, so depositing it with him is allowed. If it was already made ready, depositing it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a sign that the earlier answer is being dropped
It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
Were made ready to receive טומאה by getting wet

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the solution from how the produce is stored to the state of the produce itself, and this answer is used again in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is not difficult;
here, it is about produce that was made ready to receive טומאה,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that forbids leaving תרומה with a כהן who is an עם הארץ.

phrases.english: there, it is about produce that was not made ready to receive טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the sealed-vessel answer that Step 5 knocked down, as a new answer to the contradiction in Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different kind of produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות talk about the same produce, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Produce not yet ready to receive טומאה may be deposited with the כהן. Produce that is already ready may not.

steps.title: A משנה says wheat at an ignorant miller loses its purity status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in דמאי: wheat brought to a כותי or עם הארץ miller stays trusted for מעשר and שביעית, but not for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: Someone who brings wheat to a כותי miller or to a miller who is an עם הארץ, the wheat keeps its trusted status for מעשר and שביעית, but not for טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction from a משנה. It suggests that leaving produce with an עם הארץ does make it lose its pure status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes the miller did not swap the grain, so the מעשר and שביעית status stays. But it does worry that he touched the wheat and made it טמא. This seems to clash with the ברייתא that lets you leave produce with someone suspected about טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set one source against another, raising a contradiction
A Samaritan
A trusted, assumed status that stays until shown otherwise
Tithes

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The source is a משנה in דמאי 3:4.

phrases.english: One who brings wheat to a Samaritan miller
or to a miller who is an עם הארץ,
these keep their trusted status
for tithes and for שביעית,
but not for טומאה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that seems to clash with the lenient ברייתא as explained by רבי ירמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that allows leaving produce with someone suspected about טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says produce left with an עם הארץ loses its pure status, so depositing should not be allowed.

steps.title: No contradiction: we already said that ברייתא is about produce not ready for impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the contradiction. The lenient ברייתא was already explained as talking about produce that cannot become טמא yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of contradiction is this? Didn't we already explain that it is talking about produce that was not made ready to receive טומאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 7 by pointing back to רבי ירמיה's answer in Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא is about produce that was never made ready, so nobody can make it טמא. The משנה in דמאי worries about טומאה, so it must be talking about produce that is already ready to receive טומאה. Since they talk about different produce, they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: What contradiction is there? A way of saying the challenge is not real
We already set it up as talking about a certain case

steps.whatToRemember: After רבי אילעא's sealed-vessel answer fails because of a נדה moving the vessel, רבי ירמיה splits the cases. Produce not yet ready to receive טומאה may be left with a suspected כהן. Produce already ready may not. This also explains the משנה in דמאי.

phrases.english: What kind of contradiction is this?
Didn't we explain it as produce that was not made ready to receive טומאה?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי ירמיה's answer in Step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away the contradiction from Step 7 by using the split from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing back to a case split that was already made
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in דמאי and the lenient ברייתא are talking about the same kind of produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is about produce not yet ready to receive טומאה. The משנה is about produce that is already ready, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Why was the miller source quoted at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the earlier questioner brought the miller משנה, since its point about טומאה was already answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who raised this source, why did he raise it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask why someone quoted the miller משנה from דמאי, since its point about טומאה turned out not to be a real problem. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the גמרא said the טומאה issue was already solved. So quoting that משנה seems pointless, and the גמרא wants to know its real purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a question or challenge
What / why

phrases.english: And the one who raised it,
phrases.notes: This means whoever brought up the miller משנה from step 7.

phrases.english: why did he raise it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 8 removed the טומאה problem, the גמרא asks what the source was really for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real purpose of quoting the miller משנה.

steps.title: The miller source sets up a contradiction about switching
steps.stepSummary: The source was quoted because it says we do not worry the miller switched the wheat, and that clashes with another משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he wanted to contrast it with another source: the משנה says the wheat stays in its presumed status for מעשר and שביעית, so we do not worry that the miller switched it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the miller משנה was quoted for its other point, that we trust the wheat for מעשר and שביעית. This sets up a contradiction from a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miller משנה shows we are not afraid an עם הארץ will swap our wheat for his own untithed wheat. That point will now be tested against a source that does worry about swapping.

keyTerms.meaning: To raise a contradiction between sources
Presumed status; we assume things stay as they were
Tithes taken from produce
Laws of the seventh, שמיטה, year
To switch or swap

phrases.english: Because he wanted
to set another source against it:
these remain in their presumed status
phrases.notes: This is the miller משנה from step 7 talking about the wheat.

phrases.english: for tithes and for the seventh year,
and we are not concerned about switching.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִירְמֵי אַחֲרִיתִי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 and sets up the coming contradiction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source was quoted for its rule that we do not worry about switching.

steps.title: The mother-in-law case: we do worry about switching
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a man must tithe food he gives his mother-in-law and food he gets back, because she may switch spoiled food.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it: one who gives food to his mother-in-law must tithe what he gives her and what he takes from her, because she is suspected of switching food that went bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that contradicts the miller: with a mother-in-law, we do worry she switched the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the miller we trust the wheat stayed the same. With the mother-in-law we assume she may have swapped it for her own untithed food. So which is it: do we worry about switching or not?

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it; introduces a contradicting source
His mother-in-law
Suspected
Food that went bad

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
One who gives food to his mother-in-law,
must tithe what he gives her
and what he takes back from her,
because she is suspected
of switching what went bad!
phrases.notes: If his food spoils, she might quietly replace it with her own food, which may not be tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the contradicting source promised in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The miller rule that we do not worry about switching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mother-in-law משנה does worry about switching, so the two sources seem to clash.

steps.title: The mother-in-law has a special reason to switch
steps.stepSummary: The mother-in-law switches because she wants her daughter to eat well and is embarrassed to tell her son-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because of the reason the משנה gives. רבי יהודה said: she wants what is good for her daughter, and she is embarrassed in front of her son-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the mother-in-law is a special case with her own reason to switch the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She does not want her daughter eating spoiled food, but she is too embarrassed to tell her son-in-law his food went bad. So she quietly swaps it. That reason does not apply to a miller, so normally we do not worry.

keyTerms.meaning: As the reason is taught in the source itself
What is good for her daughter
Embarrassed

phrases.english: There, it is because of the reason that is taught:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
She wants what is good for her daughter,
and she is embarrassed in front of her son-in-law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a special motive applies only to the mother-in-law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every עם הארץ is suspected of switching food he is given.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the mother-in-law, with her special motive, is suspected; normally we do not worry.

steps.title: The innkeeper case: suspected even without family ties
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: an innkeeper is also suspected of switching, so the worry is not only about a mother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with ordinary people we are not worried? But we learned: one who gives food to an innkeeper must tithe what he gives her and what he takes from her, because she switches it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 12 by bringing an innkeeper, who has no family reason, yet is also suspected of switching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said only a mother-in-law switches, because of her feelings for her daughter. But the innkeeper משנה suspects an ordinary person too. So it seems the worry is general after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And in general / with ordinary people
Innkeeper (a woman who runs an inn)

phrases.english: And in general we are not concerned?!
But we learned: One who gives food to an innkeeper,
must tithe what he gives her
and what he takes back from her,
because she switches it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְעָלְמָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן וְהָתְנַן הַנּוֹתֵן לַפּוּנְדָּקִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 12 that only a mother-in-law is suspected.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that switching is a worry only in the special mother-in-law case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An innkeeper has no family motive, yet the משנה still suspects her of switching.

steps.title: The innkeeper also has her own reason to switch
steps.stepSummary: The innkeeper talks herself into it: why should the student eat hot food while she eats cold food?
steps.simpleTranslation: There, she tells herself it is allowed and says: should the yeshiva student eat hot food while I eat cold food?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the innkeeper also has a special reason: she convinces herself that swapping is fair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She keeps the fresh hot food for herself and gives the guest her older cold food, telling herself it is fine. Like the mother-in-law, she has a personal motive. A miller has no such motive, so normally we still do not worry about switching.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules for herself that it is allowed
A yeshiva student
Hot food
Cold food

steps.whatToRemember: Normally we do not worry that someone switched the food we gave him, like the miller. We only worry when the person has a special reason: the mother-in-law who wants to protect her daughter, or the innkeeper who justifies taking the better food.
steps.confusionAlert: The innkeeper is not called a thief here. The point is that she convinces herself it is fair, so she might swap without thinking it is wrong.

phrases.english: There, she rules it allowed for herself and says:
Should the yeshiva student eat hot food,
while I eat cold food?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 13 by giving the innkeeper her own special motive.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the innkeeper also has a personal motive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The innkeeper case shows that everyone is suspected of switching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The innkeeper is a special case too; ordinarily we are not concerned about switching.

steps.title: Are ordinary people really never suspected of switching food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that only special people, like a mother-in-law or an innkeeper, are suspected of switching food. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to worry about an ordinary neighbor too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, are we really not worried about ordinary people at all? But a ברייתא teaches: the wife of a חבר may grind together with the wife of an עם הארץ when she is טמאה, but not when she is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether we truly have no worry about regular people switching or sharing food. It brings a ברייתא that seems to show we do worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 14 gave special reasons why a mother-in-law and an innkeeper might switch food. That suggests ordinary people are trusted. But this ברייתא limits when a careful woman (the wife of a חבר) may work next to a less careful woman (the wife of an עם הארץ), so some worry about ordinary people seems to exist.

keyTerms.meaning: And still / But even so. It introduces a new difficulty.
In general, meaning ordinary people and not only special cases
A person who is careful about טהרה and tithes
A person who is not careful about טהרה and tithes
Grinds grain
Ritually impure / ritually pure

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling sounds backwards: she may grind when she is טמאה but not when she is טהורה. The ברייתא gives the rule here without a reason, so just note the surprising direction for now.

phrases.english: And still, in general are we not concerned?!
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: the wife of a חבר may grind
together with the wife of an עם הארץ
at a time when she is impure,
phrases.notes: "She" is the wife of the חבר.

phrases.english: but not at a time when she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering about the innkeeper, the גמרא questions the broader assumption that ordinary people are not suspected at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from step 10 that we generally do not worry about switching, with only special exceptions like the mother-in-law and the innkeeper.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא places limits on a careful woman working beside an ordinary, less careful woman. That suggests there is a general worry even about regular people.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids grinding together even when she is impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a stricter opinion. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the wife of a חבר may not grind with the wife of an עם הארץ even when she is טמאה, and he begins to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: even when she is impure she should not grind, because her friend...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא, now bringing the stricter view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. His reason begins here and is finished in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allowed grinding together at least when she is טמאה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids it entirely. He blames the other woman ("her friend"), and this is what makes the challenge sharp, because the worry is about what an ordinary neighbor might do.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
She should not grind
Her friend or companion, meaning the wife of the עם הארץ

steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion is the real force behind the challenge. It shows a worry about an ordinary woman's behavior, not just a mother-in-law's or an innkeeper's.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה לֹא תִּטְחוֹן,
phrases.english: Even at a time when she is impure, she should not grind,
because her friend

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה לֹא תִּטְחוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 15 and adds the stricter opinion that powers the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That we do worry about ordinary people, not only special cases like a mother-in-law or an innkeeper.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the ברייתא, which forbids grinding together even when she is טמאה because of what her friend may do.
